running_heads.head: Napoleonische Kriege / Feldzug 1815.
running_heads.reason: Pages 489 and 490 print the running head 'Krieg auf der Pyrenäischen Halbinsel — Befreiungskriege.' (checked on the page images). Every entry on them is dated 1815 and continues the 1815 campaign of pp. 486-488, whose head is 'Feldzug 1815.'

entries.reason: Bodart names only the surrendering side: 'Die österreichische Garnison (1.500 M.) übergibt den Platz ... unter der Bedingung, während dieses Krieges nicht gegen Frankreich zu dienen.' The force it surrendered to was therefore French.

The year is printed '1905' (checked on the page image). The entry stands between entries of 31./10. and 4./11. 1805 under 'Dritter Koalitionskrieg — Feldzug 1805' and names Masséna against the Austrians.

Saalfeld (10./10. 1806), French against Prussians and Saxons, opens the 1806 campaign against Prussia. Page 371's head names only the war against England and Naples ('Krieg gegen England und Neapel — Feldzug 1806'), whose Gaëta entry precedes it on the page; Jena and Auerstädt follow on pp. 372-373 under 'Krieg gegen Preußen und Rußland'.

French against a Neapolitan garrison in Calabria (18./12. 1806 to 6./2. 1807), part of the war against England and Naples with Campo Tenese, Maida and Gaëta (pp. 370-371, 'Krieg gegen England und Neapel'). Bodart prints it by its end date on p. 379, whose head names only the war against Prussia and Russia.
A Russian fleet against a Turkish fleet ('Sieg einer russischen Flotte ... über eine türkische Flotte'). Bodart lists it in the 1807 campaign, but neither side is France or fighting with it.

A British attack on Copenhagen. Bodart's text says Denmark was then only preparing an alliance with France and Russia ('Als Dänemark ... Anstalten traf, mit Frankreich und Rußland ein Offensiv- und Defensivbündnis zu schließen'), so neither side was France or fighting with it.

The unsuccessful siege of Riga (24./7. to 18./12. 1812), Russians against French, Prussian, Polish, Westphalian and Bavarian troops, belongs to the 1812 campaign against Russia. Bodart prints it by its end date on p. 446, whose head names the Peninsular War and the Befreiungskriege.
The year is printed '1809' (checked on the page image). The entry stands between 1813 entries under 'Befreiungskriege' and names Schwarzenberg's Allies against the French under Napoleon I.

Toulouse (10./4. 1814): Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese and Spanish army against Soult, the end of the campaign carried from the Peninsula into France (Orthez, B474b, is on a page headed with the Peninsular War). Page 481's head names only the Befreiungskriege.

The siege of Bayonne (23./2. to 18./4. 1814): Anglo-Portuguese and Spanish troops under Hope against the French garrison, in the same campaign as Orthez and Toulouse. Page 482's head names only the Befreiungskriege.

Austrians against Murat's Neapolitans in 1815. Bodart places the Neapolitan entries in the 1815 campaign, in which Naples fought France's opponents. Side A is the Neapolitans; no French troops are named.
Austrians against a Neapolitan garrison in 1815, in Bodart's 1815 campaign (see B485b). Side A is the Neapolitans; no French troops are named.
